To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the beta band response to a sound is modulated by both expectation and attention; 2) expectation and attention jointly influence this response; and 3) this joint modulation of sensory activity is already present before the sound is presented.
temporal expectations and attention jointly modulated the neural response to auditory stimuli in the beta band.

the neural response to a tone is modulated by expectation and attention in opposite directions: when a tone is expected and unattended, neural response decreases, but when it is attended, the effect of expectation on neural response is reversed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of temporal expectation and attention, and their effects on the neural response to sensory stimuli.
how the brain responds to a sound.
understanding how our expectations influence our perception of the world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

temporal expectation and attention can act in a synergistic fashion to enhance neural responses to expected events when attention is focused on them, and to suppress responses to unexpected events when attention is diverted.
expectation and attention act in opposite directions, with expectation decreasing neural activity in sensory regions when it is unattended, but increasing it when it is attended.

expectation and attention act in an antagonistic manner in the beta band, where expectation decreases the amplitude of the oscillatory response to an attended stimulus, but increases it to an unattended stimulus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neural response to a sensory event is influenced by the interaction of endogenous factors, such as expectation and spatial attention, in a way that is dependent on the timing of the stimulus.
expectation and attention act in opposite directions on sensory responses.
expectation and attention act jointly to modulate auditory beta band activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
expectation and attention are not necessarily antagonistic.
expectation and attention can act in opposite directions depending on whether they are directed at the same stimulus.
the effects of expectation and attention on sensory processing may not be as opposite as previously thought.
